day.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.
day.readme: Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.

day.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
day.readme: My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy.

LZ4 - Extremely fast compression LZ4 is a lossless compression algorithm, providing compression speed > 500 MB/s per core, It features an extremely fast decoder, with speed in multiple GB/s per core, typically reaching RAM speed limits on multi-core systems. new.description: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
new.readme: dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person. It is also a way of working with an agent: take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.

new.description: Craft Anything: understand how any software works, and craft your own.
new.readme: See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust. Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools, has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it. A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

new.description: Say cheese! Star this repo and your profile picture gets printed out on a receipt printer.
new.readme: Star this repo to have your GitHub profile picture framed, printed out on my receipt printer, and stuck to my wall. GitHub allows you to create webhooks for specific events on your repos, I've set one up for starring this project. When that happens, a payload is POSTed to a Cloudflare tunnel domain, which leads to a PHP script running on a Raspberry Pi that's sitting on my desk. From the inbound request, you can gleen info about the person who starred the repo, like their display name and avatar URL.

new.description: Pika H3 Flex: video and audio generation inference

new.readme: RuiC-PoseAtlas 是一个完全静态、零依赖的三图鉴参考站，把「人体怎么摆」「衣服怎么穿」「脸长什么样」三件事放在同一个站点里： 姿势图鉴：288 组 AI 生成的去脸人台姿势，每组提供 正面、斜侧、侧面、俯视、仰视 五个视角，共 1,439 张参考图。以「姿态」为单位组织，同一组的五个角度收进一张卡片，打开大图后可以用方向键连续切换，体态、比例、镜头关系一眼可比。 三者合起来的用法很直接：姿势定骨架，衣装定皮相，人像定脸。 先在姿势图鉴里挑一个机位和体态，再去衣装图鉴里找一套同气质的搭配，最后从人像图鉴里选一张脸作为角色参考，三份参考一起丢进生图工具。 很多参考图库的问题是：图片分散、视角不统一、难以把同一姿态的不同角度放在一起比较，服装更是只有一张成品图、说不清到底穿了什么。这个项目以「姿态」「衣装」和「人像」为单位重新组织了三批数据，并为衣装补上了中英日三语标签，让检索这件事真正可用。 同时，它也是一个可以独立部署的前端作品：纯 HTML + CSS + ES Modules，没有框架、没有打包器、没有运行时依赖。克隆下来用一个静态服务器打开即可；需要部署时，直接交给 GitHub...

threats.headline: vLLM passes untrusted image bytes to Pillow, enabling Ghostscript command execution on vulnerable hosts.
threats.summary: The same path also exposes a separate Pillow denial-of-service condition that can exhaust media-loading workers.
actions: Restrict who can reach image-capable vLLM endpoints.

action_quotes.quote: API-key authentication and network access controls determine who can reach the request path.

who: hosts with a vulnerable Ghostscript build

threats.title: vLLM SHM multimodal cache allows forged handles to reach pickle
threats.headline: Authenticated vLLM callers can forge SHM cache handles to run arbitrary Python in worker processes.
threats.summary: When the SHM multimodal processor cache is enabled, vLLM treats an address and monotonic_id pair as authority to read shared memory in the worker. A caller can forge this pair through public HTTP routes so the worker unpickles attacker-staged bytes. This lets an ordinary authenticated inference caller execute arbitrary Python in the worker process, even with insecure serialization disabled.
actions: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.

action_quotes.action: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.
action_quotes.quote: When --mm-processor-cache-type shm is enabled, vLLM's multimodal SHM cache represents a cached item with an address and monotonic_id pair and treats that pair as authority to dereference shared memory in the worker.

who: vLLM deployments using SHM multimodal caching
threats.quote: An ordinary authenticated inference caller can execute arbitrary Python in the worker process on a deployment that uses SHM multimodal caching.

items.connection: OpenAI's pipeline produced patches for 948 kernel privilege-escalation bugs, and Patch the Planet routes such findings to maintainers, but vendors on forked kernels sit outside that path.
items.context: routers, medical and industrial devices often ship long-lived forked Linux kernels
chain: 948 validated local privilege-escalation patches enter the upstream kernel pipeline through coordinated disclosure.
Patch the Planet connects upstream maintainers, but device vendors running old forks must work out which patches apply to them.
Each public fix becomes a map to unpatched bugs in vendor kernels, raising exposure for devices that lag.
Security consultancies can sell backport triage that matches upstream fixes to vendor trees, and regulators of medical devices will ask for proof.
items.who: Embedded device vendors and their customers benefit; vendor security teams and product compliance budgets pay consultancies.
items.variable: days from upstream fix to patched device firmware
items.versus: Waiting for distro updates does nothing for custom forks, and existing SCA tools flag versions, not whether a specific patch applies.
items.smallest_test: Take one vendor kernel fork and check the first batch of published fixes from this effort against it; success if a coding agent correctly classifies applicability for at least 80% of a hand-verified sample.
items.disconfirm: Few of the fixes touch code present in typical vendor forks, so the backport load stays small.
